key_insight: Lift4D unifies monocular 3D estimation and 4D reconstruction by using single-view priors not just as an initialization, but as a continual source of guidance during dynamic scene reconstruction. This helps bridge the gap between data-driven prediction and evidence-based refinement for non-rigid objects in the wild.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of reconstructing dynamic, non-rigid objects from monocular video, where methods must combine limited visual observations with strong geometric and appearance priors. Existing approaches either over-rely on scarce 4D training data or use priors only at the start, leaving later deformation and refinement underconstrained.
method: Start from a single-view 3D estimate to provide a strong geometric prior for the object.
Propagate and harmonize that prior through time to support 4D reconstruction from monocular video.
Refine geometry and appearance using video evidence while keeping the representation aligned with learned single-view cues.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical route to more robust 4D reconstruction without depending entirely on large-scale 4D supervision. It is especially useful for real-world dynamic scenes where data is limited, noisy, and highly non-rigid.

paper_title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild
paper_authors: Yehonathan Litman, Xiaoxuan Ma, Manan Shah, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Kris Kitani
